lines.say: Chapter one. The bank on the island.
According to the Justice Department, Stanford began operating the bank in nineteen eighty-five on Montserrat, in the British West Indies, under the name Guardian International Bank.

lines.say: He moved the bank to Antigua. In nineteen ninety-four it became Stanford International Bank. Antigua knighted him. Sir Allen Stanford, he said, was good marketing.
lines.show: He moved the bank to Antigua. In 1994 it became Stanford International Bank. Antigua knighted him. "Sir Allen Stanford," he said, was good marketing.

lines.say: The product was simple. Certificates of deposit that paid more than CDs at American banks. From Houston, financial advisers at his firm, Stanford Group Company, sold them to American investors.

scene.src: Brief of the United States, 5th Cir. No. 12-20411, Mar 3, 2015

lines.say: By the end of two thousand eight, according to the S.E.C., the bank had sold about eight billion dollars of these CDs, and claimed fifty thousand clients in more than one hundred countries. The S.E.C. called it a massive Ponzi scheme.
lines.show: By the end of 2008, according to the SEC, the bank had sold about $8 billion of these CDs, and claimed 50,000 clients in more than 100 countries. The SEC called it a massive Ponzi scheme.

lines.say: Chapter two. The paper trail.

Every year, the bank's annual report showed a profit. According to the chief financial officer, James Davis, Stanford told him the bank never had a profitable year after nineteen eighty-six. Each year, the two men made up the numbers.
lines.show: Every year, the bank's annual report showed a profit. According to the chief financial officer, James Davis, Stanford told him the bank never had a profitable year after 1986. Each year, the two men made up the numbers.

scene.src: Brief of the United States, 5th Cir. No. 12-20411, Mar 3, 2015

lines.say: The S.E.C. described the method. Each month, a predetermined return. Then the bank's accountants reverse-engineered the financial statements to match it.

scene.title: “reverse-engineered”
scene.src: SEC First Amended Complaint, N.D. Tex., Feb 27, 2009
